name: Murdaigean
summary: A dark wood of webs, goblins and wolves around Dun Murdaigean, where the renegade chieftain driven out of Thidranki took a new name (25-29).

facts.text: Murdaigean is the battleground for levels 25 to 29 (region 251); level is the only limit in Offline DAoC.
Its central keep is Dun Murdaigean; an Albion, a Midgard and a Hibernia portal keep stand at the same three places as in the other battlegrounds.
Dun Murdaigean starts neutral in the release world.
Thidranki, Murdaigean and Caledonia were the classic battlegrounds; Abermenai came with patch 1.62 (June 2003).

Its monsters are spiders, large bloated spiders, death spiders, corpse crawlers, ire wolves and rage wolves (the Angered faction), water badgers, and goblin crawlers and watchers of the Black Mountains Goblins faction (levels 13-29).

The wood, the Spider Summer and the chieftain's two names are Living Server lore.

story:
Murdaigean is the dark field, a wood where the light comes down green and goes out early, and every field-hand who has served there says the trees are closer together than when they came.

The wood. The bards of Hibernia give the name in their own tongue and say it was a holy wood once, where the people of the west kept their dead in the branches until the birds had cleaned them. The webs came later. Nobody keeps their dead in Murdaigean now, and the corpse crawlers that root among the trees are said to be what is left of the old custom: things that came for the bones and stayed when the bones ran out. The spiders are worse, large and bloated and patient, and the realms' foresters say a death spider's web across a path is the wood's way of saying the path is closed.

The goblins. In the first summer of the fields a band of goblins came into the wood from the east, out of the Black Mountains of Albion, and dug in along the southern edge, where they still crawl and watch. Albion says they were driven out of the mountains by Albion's own wardens and that the wood is welcome to them. Hibernia says Albion sent them. The goblins have never said anything a realm could understand, except, the watchers' cry at dusk, which every recruit who has served in Murdaigean learns to dread.

The chieftain of two names. In the second winter of the fields, when the renegades left Thidranki Faste under three sieges at once, their chieftain walked south and east in the snow with whoever would follow him and came to Dun Murdaigean, an old fort on a rise in the middle of the wood, held by renegades of its own. Its chieftain was dead that winter, nobody says how, and the man from Thidranki took the keep and its name, as every renegade chieftain takes the name of the keep he holds. The renegades of the wood are the strongest of the three fields' renegade garrisons after Caledon's, and the realms say that is because they are led by a man who has already lost one keep and does not mean to lose another. His guardians are many, and his commanders stand close to the walls.

The Spider Summer. In the fourth summer of the fields the webs closed the road from the Hibernian portal keep to the dun. For a whole season no recruit of any realm reached the keep from the west, and the renegades held it unchallenged, and the wolves, the ire wolves and the rage wolves of the deep wood, grew bold on what the webs let go. It ended when the three realms' foresters burned the road open in the autumn, the second thing the realms ever did in the same week. The wood grew back. It always does.

Why it matters. Murdaigean is the field where the realms' young stop being recruits and start being soldiers. The bards say that the young who come out of the wood come out older than five years should have made them.
legend: Murdaigean is the 25-29 battleground: a dark wood with Dun Murdaigean on a rise in the middle. The renegades are serious here, a lot of Renegade Guardians at 32 with rangers and commanders, under Renegade Chieftain Murdaigean at 39, so bring a full group and siege gear if you want the keep; the three Siege Masters stand at the portal keeps. The wood is full of aggressive spiders, corpse crawlers and wolves, and the goblins along the southern edge, so stay on the roads and do not fight in the trees if you can help it. Players call it Murd, say it is the darkest field, and swear the old Thidranki chieftain runs Dun Murdaigean now under a new name. Old hands remember the season the spiders closed the west road.

firstEntry: The light comes down green and goes out early.
Webs between the trees, thick as sailcloth.
Something in the branches is watching the road.
An old fort stands on a rise in the middle of the wood.
Far off, a goblin watcher cries at the dusk.

loremaster.intro: Murdaigean? The dark field. The [wood] was holy once, and the [corpse crawlers] still root for its dead. Since then the [goblins] have come in from the Black Mountains, the [Spider Summer] has come and gone, and [Dun Murdaigean] has a [chieftain of two names]. It is where the [proving fields] make soldiers of recruits.

topics.proving fields: The four contested fields away from the great frontier: Abermenai, Thidranki, [Murdaigean] and Caledon. Murdaigean is the third, for soldiers of 25 to 29.
topics.murdaigean: A dark wood with an old fort on a rise in the middle, [Dun Murdaigean]. The bards give its name in their own tongue and say the [wood] was holy.
topics.wood: The bards of Hibernia say the people of the west kept their dead in the branches of Murdaigean until the birds had cleaned them. Nobody keeps their dead there now. The webs and the [corpse crawlers] came after.
topics.corpse crawlers: Things that came to the [wood] for the bones of the old dead and stayed when the bones ran out. They root among the trees still.
topics.goblins: A band of goblins that came into the wood out of Albion's Black Mountains in the first summer of the fields and dug in along its southern edge. Albion says it drove them out; Hibernia says Albion sent them. Their watchers cry at dusk.

topics.spider summer: The fourth summer of the fields, when webs closed the road from the Hibernian portal keep to the dun for a whole season and the deep-wood wolves grew bold. The three realms' foresters burned the road open in the autumn. The [wood] grew back.

book.title: The Green Dark, by Cobthach of the Path, ranger of Tir na Nog
pages: I was a ranger of the Path for twenty years before I was sent to teach the young in Murdaigean, and I tell you plainly that I have never been in a wood I liked less. The light comes down through the leaves green and thin and goes out an hour before it should. My grandmother told me the people of the west once kept their dead in these branches, wrapped in bark, until the birds had made clean bones of them, and that the wood was holy then. I believe her. A holy place that has been forgotten is the worst kind of place.

The crawlers that root among the trees are pale and blind and many-legged, and I am told by the druids that they came for the old bones and stayed when the bones ran out. The spiders came after the crawlers, and they are patient in a way I do not like in anything. When a death spider spins across a path, the foresters say, the wood has closed the path, and they do not walk it until the web is down. In the fourth summer they closed the whole west road. I spent that summer cutting webs and burying recruits.

On the south edge there are goblins, out of the Black Mountains of Albion, which the Albions say they drove out and we say they sent. I have watched them. They dig, and they watch, and at dusk their watchers cry out in a voice I would not have believed a goblin had, and the young ones in my charge learn to hate the sound. We burned the west road open in the autumn of that summer, the three realms' foresters in the same week without a word between us, and I counted it the second miracle of the fields.

The fort in the middle of the wood is held by deserters, and their chieftain is a man who has lost a keep before. He came to Murdaigean from Thidranki in the snow, they say, and found the old chieftain dead and took his name with the keep. I met him once, under a white cloth, to bring back our dead. He was courteous and tired and he asked after the hill at Thidranki as a man asks after a house he grew up in. When I told him the Faste had no lord he laughed, and said that was the only lord it deserved.

albion.story: Albion tells Murdaigean as the goblin wood. Albion's wardens of the Black Mountains say they drove the goblins out of the mountains in the first summer of the fields and that the goblins fled west into the wood; Albion's recruits are told the goblins of Murdaigean are Albion's old enemy and are proud to kill them first. Albion's squires call the field the Webwood.
albion.legend: Albion players say the goblins on the south edge are their own leftovers from the Black Mountains, and kill them on principle. They also say Hibernia started the story that Albion sent them, which Hibernia denies.

lore: albs say they drove the murd goblins out of the black mountains. [hibs say we sent them|we didnt send them]

midgard.story: Midgard's skalds call Murdaigean the wolf wood and sing of the Spider Summer as the season the wolves grew fat. They say the rage wolves and ire wolves of the deep wood are the true lords of Murdaigean and that the renegades and goblins are only guests; Midgard's recruits are taught to read wolf sign before they are taught the roads. Midgard remembers the chieftain of two names as a man who ran from three sieges, and has no respect for him.
midgard.legend: Midgard players say the wolves in Murd are the real danger, more than the renegades, and that a Midgard group always knows where the wolves are. They call the renegade chief the runner, after the Faste Winter.

lore: skalds call murd the wolf wood. [the wolves are the real lords|the wolves own it]

hibernia.story: Hibernia's bards say Murdaigean is theirs by its name and by its dead: the people of the west kept their dead in its branches when it was holy, and the bards sing that the old dead are still somewhere in the high boughs, watching the realms fight in their wood. Cobthach of the Path's account is read to every Hibernian recruit before Murdaigean. Hibernia's foresters burned the west road open after the Spider Summer, and say the others only helped.
hibernia.legend: Hibernians say the west road is theirs because their foresters burned it open, and that you should never cut a branch in Murd, because the old dead are up there. Nobody cuts branches in Murd anyway.

lore: the bards say the old dead are still in the murd branches. [never cut a branch there|dont look up]
